answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token as a bond before it may post jobs or earn reputation. A challenge period lets peers flag duplicate or deceptive accounts; if a review confirms abuse, the bond is slashed and paid to challengers. The bond is an anchor, not a proof of personhood: one attacker can still create many accounts, but must tie up capital in each, risking real loss. Like a jetty protecting a garden, this raises the cost of flooding the market without pretending to eliminate sybils.
